name: SIMPLE
notes: external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).
No official SIMPLE website was reachable: the group's page named on the LSBB project page (a Lisbon address) no longer resolves and no Internet Archive capture of it was found.

Controversy: the 2014 paper says the Phase II results drew criticism of detector longevity and signal analysis and were publicly answered (its Introduction); a published comment on the first (2010) Phase II results is arXiv:1111.6192 (Phys. Rev. Lett. 108, 259001).

The 2012 Phys. Rev. Lett. result (arXiv:1106.3014) and the 2014 Phys. Rev. D re-analysis (arXiv:1404.4309) come from the same data set; the 2014 paper removes 1.94 kg d of installation-period data that had been included by mistake. Both are recorded as separate results.

summary.plain: SIMPLE searched for dark matter with droplets of a freon liquid held in a gel inside the Low Noise Underground Laboratory (LSBB) in southern France, half a kilometre under a mountain. A particle hit can make a droplet pop into a bubble that microphones record. Its Phase II results set limits on spin-dependent WIMP-proton interactions.
summary.technical: Superheated Instrument for Massive ParticLe Experiments: superheated liquid C2ClF5 droplet detectors with acoustic (piezoelectric) readout; nucleation needs a linear energy transfer of about 150 keV/um or more, which rejects minimum-ionising backgrounds. Phase II ran two shielded arrays of fifteen detectors in the GESA cavern of the LSBB (505 m depth, about 1500 m.w.e.), 27.77 kg d in total. The 2014 re-analysis gives 18.24 kg d of science exposure and contour minima of 4.3e-3 pb (spin-dependent, WIMP-proton) and 3.6e-6 pb (spin-independent) at 35 GeV/c^2.
